_readme: Seed data for the material catalogue. Loaded by `npm run db:seed`.
HOW TO READ THE RESISTANCE VALUES
Each resistance is a dimensionless share in [0, 1]: the fraction of that
hazard's load the material resists. 0 means the full load reaches the
structure; 1 means the hazard is fully resisted.
These are DERIVED values, not figures quoted from a standard. No Indian code
publishes a 0-1 'resistance score'. Each entry's `source_reference` names the
published basis it was derived from, and the derivation is:
wind  - from the BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas of India (3rd ed., 2019) wind
vulnerability classes for the corresponding housing typology, with
design wind loading per IS 875 (Part 3): 2015. Roof typologies drive
this most: the Atlas consistently places light sheet roofing in the
highest wind-vulnerability class and RCC slabs in the lowest.
flood - from BMTPC flood vulnerability classes together with the elevation
and wet/dry floodproofing principles in FEMA P-55 Coastal
Construction Manual (4th ed.). Elevation above grade dominates.
heat  - from thermal transmittance (U-value, W/m2K) for the assembly, per
ECBC 2017 envelope tables and IS 3792. Lower U-value maps to higher
resistance; AAC and stabilised earth score well, bare RCC poorly.
`relative_cost_index` is indexed so the conventional baseline option for each
component is 1.0. It ranks recommendations by affordability; it is NOT a price
estimate and must not be presented as one.
These derivations are a documented judgement and are listed in the README's
'Known limitations'. They should be reviewed by a structural engineer before
the tool informs a real permit decision.

materials.name: Shallow strip footing, masonry
materials.source_reference: BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas of India (3rd ed., 2019), flood vulnerability class for load-bearing masonry on shallow footings at grade; IS 1904:1986 design of foundations.
materials.notes: The conventional baseline for low-rise construction in Tamil Nadu. Sits at grade, so standing water reaches the wall base directly.

materials.name: RCC raft slab
materials.source_reference: IS 456:2000 (plain and reinforced concrete); BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas flood class for RCC raft foundations. Spreads load and resists differential settlement under saturated soil.
materials.notes: Better than strip footing against scour and saturation, but still at grade.

materials.name: RCC raft on raised plinth (600 mm above grade)
materials.source_reference: FEMA P-55 Coastal Construction Manual (4th ed.) elevation principle; National Building Code of India 2016 Part 3 plinth requirements. Elevation is the single most effective flood measure.
materials.notes: Raising the finished floor above the design flood level keeps water out of the structure entirely, which no wall material can achieve once water is inside.

materials.name: RCC pile foundation, elevated floor
materials.source_reference: FEMA P-55 open-pile foundation guidance for coastal A and V zones; IS 2911 (design of pile foundations).
materials.notes: Highest flood resistance available. Allows floodwater to pass beneath the structure. Substantially more expensive and needs a geotechnical survey.

materials.name: Stabilised compressed earth block
materials.source_reference: BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas of India flood and wind classes for earthen walling; IS 1725:2013 (stabilised soil blocks). Thermal resistance from the high thermal mass and low U-value of earth walling per ECBC 2017.
materials.notes: Excellent thermal performance and lowest cost, but earthen walling loses strength under prolonged saturation. A poor choice on a flood-exposed site despite the heat benefit.

materials.name: Fired clay brick masonry
materials.source_reference: BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas of India wind and flood classes for burnt-brick load-bearing masonry; IS 1905:1987 (structural use of unreinforced masonry). U-value per ECBC 2017 for 230 mm brick.
materials.notes: The conventional baseline for walls in Tamil Nadu. Survives inundation but absorbs water and dries slowly.

materials.name: Hollow concrete block masonry
materials.source_reference: IS 2185 (Part 1) concrete masonry units; BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas class for concrete block masonry. U-value per ECBC 2017.
materials.notes: Better wet-strength retention than fired brick. Thermal performance is slightly worse unless the cores are insulated.

materials.name: Autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC) block
materials.source_reference: IS 2185 (Part 3) autoclaved cellular concrete blocks; ECBC 2017 envelope U-value tables - AAC has roughly a quarter the thermal conductivity of fired brick.
materials.notes: The strongest heat performer among common walling options, which matters most where the binding constraint is rising wet-bulb temperature rather than wind.

materials.name: RCC shear wall construction
materials.source_reference: IS 456:2000; IS 875 (Part 3): 2015 wind load resistance for monolithic RCC; BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas lowest wind-vulnerability class for RCC framed and shear-wall construction.
materials.notes: Best structural resistance by a wide margin, but bare RCC has a high U-value and performs worst on heat unless externally insulated.

materials.name: Galvanised iron sheet roofing
materials.source_reference: BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas of India highest wind-vulnerability class for light sheet roofing; IS 875 (Part 3): 2015 uplift coefficients for light roof coverings.
materials.notes: Cheapest option and the most common failure mode in Indian cyclones: sheets lift at the fixings, after which wind and rain enter and the damage chain accelerates. Also a poor thermal performer.

materials.name: Country clay tile roofing on timber framing
materials.source_reference: BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas high wind-vulnerability class for unsecured tiled roofs on timber framing. Thermal benefit from the ventilated air gap beneath the tiles.
materials.notes: Traditional and thermally comfortable, but individual tiles are displaced by uplift well below design wind speed.

materials.name: RCC flat roof slab
materials.source_reference: IS 456:2000; BMTPC Vulnerability Atlas lowest wind-vulnerability class for RCC roof slabs. U-value per ECBC 2017 for an uninsulated 125 mm RCC slab.
materials.notes: The conventional baseline for roofing. Structurally excellent against wind; a significant heat gain path when uninsulated.

materials.name: RCC roof slab with reflective cool-roof coating
materials.source_reference: IS 456:2000 for the slab; ECBC 2017 cool-roof provisions (high solar reflectance index) for the coating. Adopted in the Telangana and Tamil Nadu cool-roof programmes.
materials.notes: Keeps the structural performance of an RCC slab and roughly doubles its heat resistance for a small cost increase. Usually the highest-value single upgrade on a heat-limited site.

materials.name: RCC sloped roof slab
materials.source_reference: IS 875 (Part 3): 2015 - a sloped monolithic roof develops lower net uplift than a flat slab of the same construction; IS 456:2000.
materials.notes: The best wind performer. Sheds water rapidly and generates less uplift than a flat slab.
